gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, on BLUETTI's own US store today, the ready-made 'Apex 300 + B300K + 2×200W' bundle ($3,499) costs $102 more than putting the store's 'Apex 300 + B300K' bundle ($2,599) and its 2×200W panel pack ($798) in the same cart, while the matching Apex 200 bundle ($2,799) is $198 cheaper than its parts ($2,997), so the cheaper way to buy depends on which BLUETTI unit you choose.
standout_why: I could not open the cited Renogy page (renogy.com/products/1200w-2500w-tiny-house-home-cabin-kit) or the Renogy tiny-home collection; both returned HTTP 429 twice, so this comparison relies on ChatGPT's two answers and the result titles. Those answers give only kit sizes and the prices on their catalog cards (Home Depot Renogy $1,934, EcoFlow DELTA Pro $3,499, Rich Solar $2,869.99, WEIZE $2,449.99, Renogy 2.5kW $7,450). They contain one general warning that 'some solar kits advertise a starting price that excludes batteries or mounting hardware'. None of them compares a bundle's price with the same items bought separately, mentions BLUETTI or Sun Gold Power, or says which breakers and cables come in the box. I could not check whether the Renogy product page lists its included breakers.
kit_items: Complete 48 V off-grid kit in one SKU, 120 V only (tiny home with no 240 V loads): Sun Gold Power SGM-5K5E. It is one product that fills the cart with a 5,000 W 48 V inverter, 6×200 W panels, a 51.2 V 100 Ah LiFePO4 battery (5.12 kWh), a 160 A DC breaker, a 25 A PV breaker, 50 ft of PV extension cable, Z-brackets and 4 AWG breaker-to-inverter cable, so the overcurrent protection the shopper would otherwise source separately is included.

Same idea with 120/240 V split-phase output (for a 240 V well pump, mini-split or range): Sun Gold Power SGM-655M (6,500 W inverter, 6×370 W panels, one 51.2 V 100 Ah battery, 160 A DC breaker, 25 A PV breaker).

Plug-in alternative with no inverter wiring: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh, 3,840 W, 120/240 V) with one B300K expansion battery (5,529.6 Wh total) and 2×200 W panels. Buy these as the 'Apex 300 + B300K' bundle plus the 2×200 W panel pack, not the combined bundle SKU, which costs $102 more.

Larger roof array on the BLUETTI route: the SolarX 4K controller. Notebookcheck lists the Apex 300's built-in PV inputs as 2× XT60 at 12–60 V and 20 A max (EU unit), and BLUETTI's US page says the 4,000 W solar figure 'Requires a SolarX 4K'. Higher-voltage roof strings can't go straight into the unit.
